messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Sometimes it is not safe to use certain medicines at the same time.
Some drugs can affect your blood levels of other drugs you use.
This may increase side effects.
This may make the medicines less effective.
If you also take sucralfate, take your furosemide dose 2 hours before or 2 hours after you take sucralfate.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
another diuretic (do not use furosemide with ethacrynic acid)
methotrexate
chloral hydrate
lithium
phenytoin
an antibiotic, especially a cephalosporin or an aminoglycoside (avoid using aminoglycosides with furosemide)
cancer medicine, such as cisplatin
cyclosporine
thyroid hormones
heart or blood pressure medicine, including ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs), such as aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may interact with furosemide.
These include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These also include vitamins and herbal products.
Triplet: ["Furosemide", "has interaction effect", "reduced effectiveness of medicines"]

The relation 'has interaction effect' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug may cause the specific pharmacological interaction effect specified by the object entity when used in combination with other drugs.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'interacts with': The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
B. 'may be prescribed with': The subject drug may be prescribed in combination with the medication specified by the object entity.
C. 'has side effect': The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
D. 'acts in': The subject drug exerts its effects within the anatomical or physiological system specified by the object entity.
E. 'similar to': The subject drug is related to or an alternative for the drug specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
